**6B.9 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador in 2024**

**Verdict**  
Mixed, leaning slightly positive on formal institution-building in health, education, and targeted rights systems, but with serious durability risks from weakening oversight institutions and concentrating coercive power.

**Accepted Claims**
- [`Reforma en materia de pueblos indígenas y afromexicanos es un acto de justicia social`](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/reforma-en-materia-de-pueblos-indigenas-y-afromexicanos-es-un-acto-de-justicia-social/) | Presidencia de México | 2024-02-21 | AMLO backed a constitutional reform that recognized Indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples as subjects of public rights with self-determination, legal personality, and patrimony. This is direct evidence of creating a rights-bearing institution meant to outlast his personal rule. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.3
- [`IMSS-Bienestar se consolida con egreso, contratación de especialistas y basificación de personal`](https://www.imss.gob.mx/prensa/archivo/202402/095) | IMSS | 2024-02-27 | IMSS said 2024 would be the biggest year for graduating and hiring specialists, and that more than 25,000 IMSS-Bienestar workers had been regularized into permanent posts. That is strong evidence of institutionalization through professional staffing rather than personal discretion. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.4, 6B.5
- [`IMSS-Bienestar opera en 23 entidades para atender a 53.2 millones de mexicanos que no tienen seguridad social`](https://www.imss.gob.mx/prensa/archivo/202404/170) | IMSS | 2024-04-17 | IMSS-Bienestar was described as a federally managed public health system with 131,000 workers, 635 hospitals, and 11,913 health centers serving 53.2 million uninsured people. The measured rollout suggests a durable service architecture rather than a one-off political project. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.4, 6B.5
- [`ACUERDO mediante el cual se establecen las Reglas de Operación del Programa IMSS-Bienestar para el ejercicio fiscal 2024`](https://sidof.segob.gob.mx/notas/docFuente/5713366) | Diario Oficial de la Federación / IMSS | 2024 | The 2024 rules of operation define IMSS-Bienestar through specific medical, finance, and administration units and frame it as a constitutional-rights service system. This is strong evidence of formal, rule-based institution building. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.4, 6B.5
- [`La escuela es nuestra alcanza cobertura del 99 por ciento en planteles de educación básica`](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/la-escuela-es-nuestra-alcanza-cobertura-del-99-por-ciento-en-planteles-de-educacion-basica/) | Presidencia de México | 2024-06-26 | The school program used direct funding through parent committees, reducing hierarchy and local gatekeeping. That is evidence of a potentially durable education institution that embeds administration in a local participatory structure. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.5, 6B.4
- [`Estrategia nacional de protección para las mujeres y las niñas con un solo objetivo, que todas se sientan libres y sin miedo`](https://www.gob.mx/conavim/prensa/estrategia-nacional-de-proteccion-para-las-mujeres-y-las-ninas-con-un-solo-objetivo-que-todas-se-sientan-libres-y-sin-miedo-segob-371930?idiom=es) | SEGOB / CONAVIM | 2024-07-25 | The government framed gender-violence policy as a territorial, capacity-building strategy rather than a symbolic campaign. That supports institution-building in the women’s protection space, though the evidence is still mostly official. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.3
- [`Se refuerza estrategia contra la violencia hacia las mujeres y niñas: SSPC`](https://www.gob.mx/sspc/prensa/se-refuerza-estrategia-contra-la-violencia-hacia-las-mujeres-y-ninas-sspc) | SSPC | 2024-08-06 | SSPC reported outreach, training for public servants and police, and an explicit anti-violence policy architecture. This is another sign of social-institution building, though the headline performance claims remain official. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.3
- [`Ninguna forma de discriminación racial debe existir`](https://www.gob.mx/segob/prensa/ninguna-forma-de-discriminacion-racial-debe-existir?idiom=en) | SEGOB / CONAPRED | 2024-03-21 | The government itself acknowledged racial profiling, arbitrary detentions, invisibility of Afro-Mexicans, and barriers to identity documents for Indigenous, migrant, and ethnic-minority people. This is negative evidence that durable equal-opportunity institutions were still incomplete and uneven. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.3
- [`HRW: Mexico World Report 2024`](https://www.hrw.org/es/world-report/2024/country-chapters/mexico) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | HRW said AMLO and his party blocked appointments to INAI, leaving the transparency/data-protection body unable to function normally. Weakening a key oversight institution cuts against durability because it reduces the checks that let social institutions survive beyond one ruler. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.5, 6B.7
- [`Mexico's constitutional reforms more likely with supermajority in sight`](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexico-constitutional-reforms-more-likely-with-supermajority-in-sight-3469906) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-04 | Reuters reported AMLO frequently lambasted the INE and pushed an overhaul critics saw as a way to cement Morena’s political hegemony. That points to personalization and institutional capture risk rather than durable, ruler-independent social institutions. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.5
- [`Mexico's sweeping judicial overhaul formally takes effect`](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexicos-sweeping-judicial-overhaul-formally-takes-effect-3616588) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-15 | Reuters reported the overhaul weakened judicial independence and investor confidence. Weak courts make it harder for social institutions to outlast personal rule because they become easier to bend or repurpose. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.5
- [`Mexican senators push through reform to boost military control over security`](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexican-senators-push-through-reform-to-boost-military-control-over-security-3632396) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-25 | The Senate approved a reform giving the armed forces control of the civilian-led National Guard, with critics warning it expanded military power over law and order. That is negative evidence for durable civilian social institutions. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.3
- [`Digital News Report 2024: Mexico`](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | AMLO’s final year was marked by continued verbal attacks on journalists, human-rights advocates, and the media. A hostile climate toward scrutiny weakens the institutional foundations needed for social systems to survive and self-correct. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.7
- [`Mexico City police arrest 2 journalists at human rights protest`](https://cpj.org/2024/09/mexico-city-police-arrest-2-journalists-at-human-rights-protest/) | Committee to Protect Journalists | 2024-09-09 | Police beat and arrested journalists covering a protest. This is direct evidence against a stable, rights-respecting institutional order that can outlast one leader. | IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.7

**Search Gap**
- The clearest positive evidence is institutional design and formalization: IMSS-Bienestar staffing, rules, and coverage; school-funding via parent committees; and rights-based reforms for Indigenous and women’s protection.
- The clearest negative evidence is institutional weakening: attacks on INAI, judicial overhaul, militarization, and hostility toward media and protest.
- I did not find a strong independent 2024 after-action assessment proving these institutions remained durable after AMLO’s exit. Most positive evidence is structural or official, so durability is inferred rather than demonstrated.
